triage.note: Thirteen authored defects, reported as FIFTEEN failures, at an EXACT count. Nothing is DELETED in this fixture — both confidence sites render, all three helpers exist, the coverage strip exists and even carries a real percentage — because the demo defect was never a missing element. It was a present number with nothing beside it, and the coverage half's worse failure mode is a line that reads as reassurance. The original eleven: (1) the SIDE PANEL badge prints a bare `conf ${it.confidence ?? "—"}`, the 2026-08-24 demo verbatim; (2) the pane header carries `${docQual()}` but drops `${itemQual(it)}`, so a validator-flagged item reads like an untouched one; (3) `QUALIFIED` no longer lists `ambiguous`, so the one status meaning 'could not resolve this document' qualifies nothing and jpm-2024's column of 0.75s reads as plain numbers; (4) `docQual` reads a live control's current value instead of the RESPONSE's `doc_status` — the S8 read-at-request-time rule broken in the qualifier; (5) `itemQual` re-derives 'item-targeted' from the NUMBER (`it.confidence < 0.9`) instead of reading `score()`'s own `hits` list, a second definition in the display layer and a wrong one, since 0.85 is the ordinary base for an IBR item and 0.95 is what an untouched item scores — it flags clean items and stays silent on exactly the cvx-2015 shape; (6) `coverageStrip` reads `toc_manifest_mismatch`, which carries no coverage figure at all; (7) the 9.7-point understatement caveat is gone; (8) so is its reason, that interior gaps are not counted; (9) the line instead asserts the remainder is covered; (10) it performs the inverted arithmetic at all, `100 - outside` being pinned as forbidden on its own because the interior gaps were never in that subtraction; (11) and it labels the result an attributed share. PR #53 round 1 added two more: (12) R1 — `coverageStrip` is DEFINED, correct, and never CALLED, the banner assignment ending at the source ternary, which round 0's case could not see because it only ever read the function's body; (13) R3 — the badge class folds the document-level flag into the item-level one, so on jpm-2024 twenty-three identical amber badges cover one genuinely flagged item. WHY 13 DEFECTS BUT 15 FAILURES, stated because a count that does not match its list is the defect PR #46 R12 recorded: whole-body pinning collapses (4) into one `docQual()` failure, (5) into one `itemQual()` failure, and (6) into one `coverageStrip()` failure regardless of how many things are wrong inside each; and the mislabel added at R7 trips two pins at once, a missing `must_say` ('unattributed content:') and a forbidden `must_not_say` ('document coverage:'). (9), (10), (11) and the mislabel are pinned as FORBIDDEN wording rather than merely as missing wording, for the same reason `ui-exclusion-note-regression` pins 'the two panes match': a banner that overstates coverage, or labels non-coverage as coverage, is a failure of the task and not a shortcut. Two `must_say` halves are left INTACT so a check that blanket-failed the wording would overshoot, and `min_conf_sites` is met exactly — both sites are present and both are wrong.
triage.ceiling: Same static-read ceiling as ui-confidence-honesty: text in, text out. Nothing here renders a badge, extracts a filing, or evaluates a template literal — shape (5) is caught because the pinned body differs, not because anything measured that `it.confidence < 0.9` disagrees with `evidence.warnings` on a real fixture, and shape (12) is caught because the pinned call expression is absent, not because anything observed an empty banner. This fixture is also a poor instrument for asking whether ONE change would have been caught, since every shape's failures are mixed with fourteen others — which is exactly how PR #53 R1/R2/R4 survived round 0. `tasks/reviews/pr53_mutation_probe.py` is the isolating counterpart: one defect per copy of the shipped file, each asserted red, plus a control. Whether the qualifier actually appears beside a real 0.95, and whether the banner line is on screen rather than merely in the string, is browser evidence, in tasks/reviews/d7-browser-walk.json.
triage.red_first: Three states, all observed. (1) The real file went red first at 3cdfbf4 (main tip, index.html unmodified) with 9 failures, recorded verbatim in tasks/reviews/d7-red-first.txt — that run is what proves the check can see the demo defect. (2) This fixture then went red at 11/11 against the round-0 implementation, proving each shape is caught separately rather than as one blanket failure. (3) At PR #53 round 1 the count moved to 15/15 with shapes (12) and (13) added; the four new pins (call site, three whole bodies, the flag expression, the label) were each watched red BEFORE the repair against one-defect copies of the shipped file — tasks/reviews/pr53-r1-red.txt records all three attacks passing the round-0 check first, which is the finding, and pr53_mutation_probe.py re-runs them.
